calls.head: Daccord is due against the Red Wings
calls.body: Daccord has been shaky against the Red Wings since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.
calls.call: If Daccord starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .907 than to his .873 against the Red Wings.

surprises.head: Detroit couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Seattle usually allows fewer dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: Detroit’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.5% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% (about 6.0% against Seattle) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

story.head: DeBrincat scores his 300th, but the Red Wings lose
paras: Mackie Samoskevich struck first for the Kraken midway through the first, and Ryker Evans stretched the lead to 2-0 on the power play early in the second. Brandon Montour made it 3-0 late in the period. Viktor Arvidsson and Lucas Raymond scored 59 seconds apart early in the third to cut Seattle’s lead to 3-2. Alex DeBrincat scored his 300th NHL goal on the power play with 17 seconds left to tie it 3-3. The shootout went four rounds, and Bobby McMann won it for the Kraken after Frédérick Gaudreau had scored earlier.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Philipp Grubauer made 22 saves for the Kraken, and Daniil Tarasov stopped 24 of 27. The Kraken improved to 6-3-1, and the Red Wings fell to 3-3-3.
